title: Sequence digital codes for degenerate residues do not match the profile emission columns
body:
Two tables in libnail number the six degenerate amino residues differently. Read at `0aae149`; no test or run confirms the effect yet.

`UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO` in `alphabet.rs` maps a sequence byte to its digital code. `Sequence::from_fasta` stores that code in `digital_bytes`, and the DP looks the code up directly with `Profile::match_score(residue, profile_idx)`, which reads `emission_scores[MATCH_IDX][profile_idx][residue]`.

`ProfileBuilder::build` fills the degenerate columns of `emission_scores` from `Alphabet::ambiguity_map()`. It walks `ambiguous_iter()`, which yields 21 to 26, and `AmbiguityMap`'s `Index` subtracts 21 because HMMER puts `-` at 20. Column 20 stays at `-inf`.

| code | sequence side (`UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO`) | profile side (`build`) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | O | gap, `-inf` |
| 21 | U | O, scored as K |
| 22 | X | U, scored as C |
| 23 | B | X, `-inf` (its canon list is empty) |
| 24 | Z | B, from N and D |
| 25 | J | Z, from Q and E |
| 26 | none | J, from I and L |

If the DP reads these as the table says, a target X scores as C, and a target O or B scores `-inf` at every match state. `AMINO_ALPHABET_WITH_DEGENERATE` follows the profile side's order (`-`, B, J, Z, O, U, X), which differs from both.

Even with the codes lined up, X keeps `-inf`, because `build` skips any entry with an empty canon list. HMMER scores X with an expected value over all residues.

X is common in MGnify: 187 of the first 100,000 sequence lines of `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-serial-overhead/order/t.fa` contain one.

## Open

- Whether the insert scores and `from_blosum_62_and_seq` hit the same mismatch.
- A test to write first: score a one-residue target X, B or O against a small profile, and compare with `hmmsearch` on the same pair.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Confirmed at `94eecda`, at the score level and end to end. Both checks used the throwaway code in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-degenerate-codes`.

At position 1 of `7tm_1`, from the first record of `fixtures/query.hmm`, `match_score(code, 1)` gives U the score of K, X the score of C, O and B `-inf`, Z the score of the B column, and J the score of the Z column. No nail code remaps `digital_bytes` between `Sequence::from_fasta` and the DP.

End to end, I took `O08892` from `fixtures/target.fa` (389 residues) and wrote one variant per degenerate residue, replacing every copy of one residue. Both tools ran without null2 (`hmmsearch --nonull2`, `nail search --no-null2`). Scores are in bits.

| variant | hmmsearch | nail | nail scored the new residue as |
|---|---|---|---|
| original | 267.1 | 267.0 | |
| all 17 K to O | 267.1 | 185.4 | `-inf` |
| all 13 C to U | 267.1 | 228.0 | K |
| all 13 C to X | 233.5 | 267.0 | C |
| all 13 N to B | 261.0 | 212.9 | `-inf` |
| all 8 Q to Z | 266.3 | 265.0 | B (N, D) |
| all 45 L to J | 263.6 | 189.5 | Z (Q, E) |

hmmsearch scores O as K and U as C. It scores B, Z and J as a mix of their canon residues, and X as a mix of all 20, since 233.5 sits below 267.1. Every degenerate residue in nail scores differently from hmmsearch.

## What a fix touches

- `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO`, `AMINO_INVERSE_MAP`, `AMINO_INVERSE_MAP_LOWER`, `to_utf8_byte_amino` and the `UPPER` string of `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO_TABLE` in `sequence.rs` would move to the `AminoAcid` order: `-` 20, B 21, J 22, Z 23, O 24, U 25, X 26.
- `Alphabet::ambiguity_map()` would list B, J, Z, O, U, X in that order, with all 20 canonical residues for X.
- Callers that index by digital code need checking: `scoring.rs` null2 (`expected_scores[target.digital_bytes[idx]]`), the consensus lookup in `nail/src/mmseqs.rs`, `cloud_search.rs` through `AminoAcid::from_u8`, and `Profile::serialize`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Sequence queries are affected too. `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq` reads `CONDITIONAL_PROB[residue]`, and that table's rows run in the `AminoAcid` order: 20 gap, all zeros, then B, J, Z, O, U, X. A query residue is looked up by its sequence code, so the wrong row comes back.

Checked with `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-degenerate-codes/src/bin/query.rs`. Each query was `ACDEFGHIKL` with position 6 changed to one degenerate letter.

| position 6 | row it got | consensus at 6 | `fwd_lambda` |
|---|---|---|---|
| G (control) | G | g | 0.9087 |
| O | gap, all zero | a | NaN |
| U | B | d | 0.9229 |
| X | J | l | 0.9249 |
| B | Z | e | 0.9276 |

An O in a query zeroes every emission probability at its position. The `p * log2(p / f)` sum then hits `0 * -inf`, which makes `fwd_lambda` NaN, and every E-value for that query becomes NaN.

Records with no degenerate letter are unaffected. The canonical codes 0 to 19 agree across every table. The mmseqs prefilter reads `utf8_bytes`, not the digital codes.
